title: Unsupervised Key Event Detection from Massive Text Corpora

problem.claim: Detect key events from news corpora at an intermediate granularity, where each event occurs at a particular time and location and focuses on the same topic.

gap.claim: Existing research emphasizes either major-theme detection or fine-grained mention-level action extraction, leaving intermediate-level key event detection insufficiently addressed; the task is also challenged by thematically and temporally close events and scarce labeled data.

contributions.claim: Introduces key event detection as an intermediate-level event understanding and structuring task.

Develops EvMine, an unsupervised framework that extracts temporally frequent peak phrases with a ttf-itf score, forms event-indicative feature sets using a peak phrase graph, and iteratively retrieves related documents using pseudo-label-trained classifiers.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments and case studies reportedly show that EvMine outperforms all baseline methods and ablations on two real-world news corpora.

narrative_sequence.summary: Automated event detection from news corpora is presented as important for mining fast-evolving structured knowledge.
Prior work is characterized as focusing on either corpus-level theme detection or document-level mention-level action extraction.
The paper proposes intermediate-level key event detection for events tied to a particular time, location, and topic.
The task is difficult because distinct key events may be thematically and temporally close, while labeled data are scarce.

EvMine combines peak-phrase extraction, graph-based feature-set construction, and iterative pseudo-label-based document retrieval; experiments and case studies report advantages over baselines and ablations on two news corpora.

source_observation.claim: The task combines signals about thematic content, time, location, and document relationships to distinguish closely related key events.

interpretation.claim: When target phenomena occupy an intermediate granularity, combining multiple complementary signals may help separate semantically adjacent instances.

application.claim: For unsupervised analysis of rapidly changing document streams, construct representations that jointly use temporal frequency, semantic similarity, and document co-occurrence.

exception.claim: This lesson may not transfer when events are not temporally evolving, when labels are abundant, or when the application requires document-level actions rather than intermediate-level events.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the two news corpora.
Quantitative results, evaluation metrics, and baseline details are not provided.
The abstract does not specify the ttf-itf formulation or implementation details.
No details are given about the automatically generated pseudo labels or iteration schedule.
